diagnostic: by printing a short, consistent message at the start and end of each major step so you can confirm execution order and control flow
by printing key input parameters and configuration values (including defaults) to ensure the code is running under the assumptions you expect
by printing shapes, lengths, and type information for important variables to quickly spot mismatches or unexpected structures
by printing representative samples of data (e.g., first/last few items, random examples) rather than entire datasets to keep output readable
by printing summary statistics for data (e.g., min/max/mean, distinct counts, missing value counts) to validate data characteristics at each stage
by printing explicit checks of method assumptions (e.g., expected ordering, uniqueness, monotonicity, normalization) and flagging when they are violated
by printing intermediate results at boundaries between components (e.g., pre/post transformation) to isolate where unexpected values first appear
by printing sentinel markers around conditional branches and loops so you can verify which paths are taken and how often
by printing error-context details when failures occur (inputs, indices, relevant identifiers) to make issues reproducible and easier to trace
by printing timing information for expensive steps (start/stop timestamps or durations) to identify performance bottlenecks without guessing
by printing resource-related indicators when relevant (e.g., batch sizes, memory-heavy object sizes, cache hits/misses) to explain slowdowns or crashes
by printing invariant assertions and their outcomes (pass/fail) to confirm that core expectations remain true throughout execution
by printing logging at multiple verbosity levels (e.g., minimal vs. detailed) so you can scale diagnostics up or down without rewriting messages
by printing identifiers for key entities (record IDs, filenames, request IDs) to correlate outputs across stages and across runs
by printing a concise final report (counts processed, successes/failures, key metrics) to validate end-to-end behavior and compare runs
